senses.gloss:
Vṛndāban
------------------------------------------
Vṛndāban (also spelt as Vṛndāvan, Bṛndāvan and Bṛndāban) is one of the famous places of पिल्ग्रिमगे closely associ-ated with the childhood days of Lord कृष्ण. It is at a distance of 10 kms. (7 miles) from the city of मथुरा (See MATHURĀ.) in Uttar Pradesh.
Though a small town on the bank of the यमुना river, it is dotted with innumerable temples, ghāṭs (places on the river bank provided with steps for taking bath) and other sacred spots connected with कृष्ण’s life.
The name वृन्दाबन् is derived from Vṛndā, the daughter of the king Kedāra, who practised severe austerities here to get Lord विष्णु as her husband. After succeeding in getting the boon from him, she was reborn here as राधा, the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu and Kalāvatī.
The following are the more important of the temples:
Kṛṣṇagopala Mandir, Baṇkebihāri Mandir, Shāḥ Bihārījī Mandir, राधा-ramaṇ Mandir, Śrīraṅgajī Mandir (of रङ्गनाथ, built in the South Indian style) and Gopāleśvaranātha Mandir (of शिव).
The famous गोकुल where कृष्ण spent his childhood days first, is on the opposite bank of the river यमुना. Of the several temples, that of Gokulnāth is the chief one.
The गोवर्धन hill which is 34 kms. (21 miles) from मथुरा is a small hillock spread over 6 to 7 kilometres (4 miles). It has an ancient temple dedicated to Govardhananātha. About 5 kms. (3 miles) away from this hill is the village Rādhākuṇḍa surrounded by two big tanks known as Rādhākuṇḍa and Kṛṣṇakuṇḍa.
